transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Yeah, hi… I guess what brings me in is, um, something happened at work that kind of got people worried. I’m a personal care aide, and we were in a staff meeting, talking about safety stuff, fall prevention and all that, and I got really worked up about it. Like, I started showing everybody what I meant instead of just saying it.

I moved the chairs around and started acting out this whole fall-prevention drill, waving my arms and stepping around like I was demonstrating how someone might fall or how we should catch it or prevent it. And I know that sounds like I was just being thorough, but it went past that. People were telling me to sit down, like, “Okay, that’s enough,” and I just… I couldn’t seem to stop right away. I kept going like my body was already in the middle of it and my mouth and arms were moving before I could think.

It was embarrassing after, because everybody was looking at me, and I could tell it wasn’t normal meeting behavior. That’s really why I’m here.
Around the time this happened, did you feel unusually high, euphoric, or excessively good?

Yeah… I mean, not like happy in a normal way exactly. It’s more like there are stretches where I feel really bright, like my head is lit up and everything is finally lining up the way it’s supposed to. I feel fired up, like I can see what needs to happen and I want to move on it right then.

But it can turn fast, too. If someone slows me down or questions what I’m saying, I get irritated—like sharper than I mean to be. I’ll snap back, and afterward I’m kind of like, why did I come at them that hard? So yes, there’s that “up” feeling, but it’s mixed with this edge, like I’m energized and touchy at the same time.
During these energized periods, do you need much less sleep than usual?

Yeah, definitely. That’s actually one of the things that feels strange after I look back at it, because in the moment I don’t feel tired the way I should.

Like I can sleep maybe two or three hours—go to bed late, or sometimes I’m just laying there with my mind still going—and then I’ll wake up before dawn, like when the house is still completely dark and quiet, and I’ll feel ready. Not rested in the normal sense, maybe, but ready to get up and start doing things. I’ll be thinking about plans, what needs fixing, what I should say to somebody, how to organize something, and it doesn’t seem odd to me at the time.

I’ll be up moving around or writing things down, making plans in my head, and part of me is like, “Well, this is good, I’m getting ahead of the day.” It’s only later that I realize most people would think being up after two hours of sleep and acting like it’s normal is… not really normal. But when I’m in it, I don’t feel like I need more sleep.
Have you had other separate times in your life when you felt this same kind of energized, needing-less-sleep state?

Yeah… it hasn’t just been this one time with the meeting. It’s been kind of coming and going for a while now. I’d say… maybe around 11 months? Close to a year, but not exactly a full year, I don’t think.

It’s not every single day straight through, which makes it confusing, because I’ll have stretches where I’m more like myself, and then it comes back—this feeling like I’m charged up, sleeping barely anything, and getting really fixed on plans or things I think need to happen right away. When I’m in it, it feels like momentum, like I’m finally getting somewhere. Then afterward I can see it was too much.

So yeah, there have been other separate times. It’s been happening off and on for about 11 months.
Have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

I… I’m not really sure how to answer that cleanly. Like, I’ve had times where I felt down, yeah, where things felt heavy and I didn’t feel like myself, but when you say at least two weeks, most of the day, nearly every day… I don’t know if I can pin it down like that.

I don’t want to say yes if I’m not remembering it right. Sometimes the days blur together, and I can tell you I’ve had low stretches, but whether it was that steady for two full weeks, I’m not sure. I’d probably need to think through it more carefully, like what was happening around that time and how long it actually lasted.
Have any of these energized periods lasted a full week or longer?

Yeah… I think so. Not like it’s been one solid block for 11 months, but these stretches where I’m really keyed up, barely sleeping, and pushing these big plans or feeling like things have to move right now — those have been coming and going for about 11 months.

As far as a full week… yeah, I’d say some of them probably have lasted that long, maybe longer. It’s hard because when I’m in it, I’m not marking days on a calendar. I’m just going, going, going, and it feels like that’s how I’m supposed to be. Then later I look back and realize, okay, that wasn’t just one bad night or a couple busy days. That was a stretch.

So yes, I think there have been times where it went on a week or more, with the little sleep and all that energy and getting really wrapped up in plans.
Have you ever had a time when, for at least two weeks, you felt depressed nearly all day every day?

I’m still not sure, honestly. I know you’re asking it pretty specifically — like two weeks, depressed nearly all day, every day — and I don’t want to just say yes because I’ve had bad patches.

There have been times where I felt really low or kind of weighed down, and when I look back some of it feels like it lasted a while, but I can’t tell you confidently that it was two full weeks like that, almost the whole day, every day. My memory of it isn’t that organized. Some days I might’ve been down in the morning and then distracted later, or I might’ve had a few rough days and then a better day, and then it came back. So I don’t know if that counts as what you’re asking.

I guess the honest answer is: I’m not sure. I’ve had low periods, but I can’t clearly say there was a solid two-week stretch where I was depressed nearly all day every day.
During one of these energized periods, did you ever hear or see things other people couldn’t, or believe something that others said wasn’t true?

Yeah… yeah, that has happened. Not every single time I got keyed up, but during some of those fired-up stretches — when I was barely sleeping, just a few hours, and I had all these plans in my head like everything had to happen right then — I would hear things that, looking back, I don’t think were really there.

The main thing was hearing calls… like hearing someone calling me or like a phone or work-related call, and then I’d check and there was nothing. Nobody else seemed to hear it. At the time, though, it didn’t feel like “maybe I’m imagining this.” It felt real, like I needed to respond or pay attention.

And I also got really sure my supervisor was setting traps for me. Like not just “he’s being unfair” or “he’s watching me,” but I mean I felt certain there were setups, like little things arranged to catch me or prove something about me. Other people would say that wasn’t what was happening, or they’d tell me I was reading too much into it, but during those periods I was convinced. It all connected in my head, especially when I was running on hardly any sleep.
Have you ever heard those calls or believed your supervisor was setting traps for you during a time when you were not feeling unusually energized or high?

Yeah… that’s the part that kind of bothers me, because it wasn’t only when I was all sped up.

There was a stretch where I wasn’t really like that — I mean, I was calmer. I was sleeping more normal, not staying up all night or running around trying to get a bunch of plans going. I wasn’t in that “everything has to happen right now” mode. But even then, for weeks, I still kept hearing my name being called sometimes. Like I’d turn my head because I was sure somebody said it, and then nobody had.

And the work thing stayed with me too. I was still convinced people were keeping notes on me at work. Not just regular paperwork, but like they were tracking me or writing things down to use later. Even when I wasn’t especially energized, that feeling didn’t really go away for a while. It was quieter, maybe, but it was still there, and I still believed it.
Have you ever had a time lasting at least two weeks when you felt depressed nearly all day, almost every day?

I think my answer is still… I don’t really know how to say yes to that, not the way you’re asking it.

I’ve had times where I felt down, like heavy or discouraged, and I know there were stretches where it felt like it dragged on. But when you say “at least two weeks” and “nearly all day, almost every day,” that’s where I get stuck. I can’t honestly look back and say, yes, it was clearly that exact kind of stretch. My memory of those periods is kind of broken up — some days I was low for part of the day, some days I might’ve been okay for a while, or just distracted, and then it would come back again.

So I don’t want to give you the wrong answer just to make it fit. I’ve definitely had low moods, but I’m not sure I’ve had a full two weeks where I was depressed almost the whole day, nearly every day.
Did the voices or those beliefs about people at work ever continue for at least two weeks when you were not feeling especially high, energized, or depressed?

Yeah… yes. That’s actually what I meant before, but I guess to answer it more straight: it did go on for more than two weeks when I wasn’t feeling especially high or energized, and I wasn’t really in a depressed stretch either.

There was this calmer period where I was sleeping more like a normal person — not perfect, but not that thing where I’m up all night with my mind racing and trying to start projects or fix everything at once. I wasn’t rushing around, I wasn’t full of all these big plans, I wasn’t feeling like I had to do everything right now. I was more slowed down, more regular, I guess.

But even during that time, for several weeks, I would still hear my name being called. It wasn’t constant all day, but it kept happening. I’d be at home or somewhere quiet and I’d turn like, “Yeah?” because I was sure someone said my name, and then there’d be nobody. And the work thing was still there too. I still believed people at work were keeping notes on me — like tracking things, writing stuff down to use against me later. It didn’t feel like just a worry. It felt like something that was happening.

So, yes… those things did continue for at least a couple weeks, probably several weeks, when I wasn’t in one of those high-energy times and I wasn’t feeling depressed nearly all day either.

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 3
target_item.manifestation: There was a calmer stretch when I was sleeping more normally and wasn't rushing around with projects, but for several weeks I still heard my name being called and stayed convinced people at work were keeping notes on me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the voices and workplace beliefs continued for at least two weeks when the patient was not high, energized, or depressed, which directly matches this item.

patient.answer:
Yeah… yes. That’s actually what I meant before, but I guess to answer it more straight: it did go on for more than two weeks when I wasn’t feeling especially high or energized, and I wasn’t really in a depressed stretch either.

There was this calmer period where I was sleeping more like a normal person — not perfect, but not that thing where I’m up all night with my mind racing and trying to start projects or fix everything at once. I wasn’t rushing around, I wasn’t full of all these big plans, I wasn’t feeling like I had to do everything right now. I was more slowed down, more regular, I guess.

But even during that time, for several weeks, I would still hear my name being called. It wasn’t constant all day, but it kept happening. I’d be at home or somewhere quiet and I’d turn like, “Yeah?” because I was sure someone said my name, and then there’d be nobody. And the work thing was still there too. I still believed people at work were keeping notes on me — like tracking things, writing stuff down to use against me later. It didn’t feel like just a worry. It felt like something that was happening.

So, yes… those things did continue for at least a couple weeks, probably several weeks, when I wasn’t in one of those high-energy times and I wasn’t feeling depressed nearly all day either.

inference.note: Psychotic symptoms persisted for several weeks outside of mood episodes, which rules out F31.2 and supports schizoaffective disorder, manic type.

opening_question.intent: Learn the patient's main reason for seeking care today
opening_question.question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes recurrent manic episodes lasting about a week or longer with elevated/irritable mood, markedly decreased need for sleep, increased activity, and disinhibited behavior. They also report psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations and persecutory delusions) occurring during mood episodes and persisting for several weeks during a period without prominent mania or depression. This pattern supports schizoaffective disorder, manic type, rather than bipolar disorder with psychotic features, because psychosis occurred for at least 2 weeks outside a mood episode. A major depressive episode was not clearly established.
